plans.note: Section 15 is captioned as a one-way limitation of Garman's liability; review cap amount, mutuality and carve-outs (IP indemnity in sec-13, confidentiality in sec-14, gross negligence/wilful misconduct). Check interaction with warranty remedies in sec-12.

Section 13 provides an IP indemnity from Garman; confirm scope (defence, costs, no cap via sec-15) and add indemnity for Garman's own misconduct/personal injury/property damage. Verify no reciprocal broad customer indemnity.
No non-compete heading; software licence deals rarely contain one. Scan restrictions on use (sec-3) and general matters (sec-20) for any covenant limiting our use of competing routing products.
Likely absent, but check grant/restrictions (sec-2, sec-3) and maintenance/fees (sec-10, sec-11) for sole-source or exclusive-supplier language for support and future modules.
No pricing-parity heading; review fees (sec-11) and maintenance fee escalation (sec-10) for any obligation running against us, and note absence of an MFN in our favour as an optional ask.

Section 19 expressly binds employee non-solicitation; check mutuality, duration (target 12 months), scope limited to individuals involved in the project, and a general-advertising carve-out; also check survival treatment in sec-18.

Section 17 governs term and termination; confirm we may terminate maintenance/licence on notice without penalty and that Garman cannot terminate at convenience mid-term. Rejection rights in sec-7/sec-8 and maintenance term in sec-10 are related exit paths.
Auto-renewal of maintenance likely sits in sec-10 or sec-17; check notice window (target 30–60 days for us) and any uncapped renewal fee uplift in sec-11.

Governing law, venue and any arbitration clause should be in general matters (sec-20); confirm it is an accepted jurisdiction with courts rather than foreign arbitration, given the US/Canada-UK party mix.

Assignment clause expected in sec-20; secure affiliate/successor assignment and licence transfer rights (interacts with the grant in sec-2) and ensure no Garman termination right on our change of control (sec-17).

Ownership statements likely in the grant/restrictions (sec-2, sec-3); confirm our data (including converted data under sec-4) and any customisations we pay for are ours, that feedback/derivative clauses do not assign our IP, and align with confidentiality (sec-14) and escrow (sec-16).

Section 2 is the grant; check it is perpetual/irrevocable on payment, extends to affiliates and contractors, and that 'Authorized Locations' and other defined limits (sec-1, sec-6) plus sec-3 restrictions are not unduly narrow.

Any usage-verification right most likely accompanies the use restrictions in sec-3 or general matters (sec-20); require notice, business-hours, once-yearly, confidentiality-protected and vendor-cost audits.

Watch for interest on late payment, penalties or forfeiture of prepaid fees in sec-11, and any damages tied to our co-operation obligations in sec-9 or termination in sec-17; conversely note absence of service credits under sec-10.

Section 12 carries specifications and warranty; check duration runs from acceptance (sec-6), that the remedy is repair/replace with refund fallback, and that maintenance obligations (sec-10) do not displace the warranty; confirm no broad disclaimer.
No insurance heading; given on-site installation and training (sec-4, sec-5, sec-9), propose commercial general liability, professional liability/E&O and cyber cover in general matters (sec-20).

Check fees (sec-11) and maintenance (sec-10) for committed multi-year maintenance, minimum seat/location counts or non-refundable prepayments, and confirm an exit aligned with sec-17 termination rights.

Termination consequences in sec-17 (and sec-8 on rejection) likely address return of software but not our data or wind-down help; escrow (sec-16) is a partial substitute. Propose transition assistance and data return, with survival added in sec-18.
